 Match Summary
 Men's World Cup Australia 28, New Zealand 6 Australia Australia Australia 28 6 New Zealand New Zealand New Zealand 2nd Half , in progress Half Time Australia 24 , New Zealand 6 HT 24-6 Tries Australia, Martin (2', 38'), Bostock (19'), Best (32'), Trbojevic (43') Martin 2 minutes, 38 minutes, Bostock 19 minutes, Best 32 minutes, Trbojevic 43 minutes New Zealand, McLean (12') McLean 12 minutes Conversions Australia, Munster (3', 33', 40') Munster 3 minutes, 33 minutes, 40 minutes New Zealand, Isaako (14') Isaako 14 minutes Penalties Australia, Munster (24') Munster 24 minutes Venue: Suncorp Stadium Live Reporting (active) 
 Line-ups 
 Summary
 Click 'listen live' button for BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 2 commentary
 Liam Martin gives Australia lead after just 85 seconds - the fastest-ever try in a Rugby League World Cup final
 Casey McLean draws New Zealand level, but Jack Bostock restores Kangaroos' lead, before Bradman Best and Martin extend it
 Tom Trbojevic adds fifth Australia try shortly after half-time
 Kangaroos won 24-22 when the teams met in epic tournament opener on 15 October

 Live Reporting
 Emma Smith
 Post published at 59 mins 59 mins 
 Australia 28-6 New Zealand 
 That was a very debatable call by the video officials, albeit probably correct by the letter of the law.
 They do rule against Australia with the next decision though, after the hosts use their Captain's Challenge claiming a late tackle.
 0 0 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 DISALLOWED TRY - Australia 28-6 New Zealand published at 10:03 GMT 10:03 GMT 
 There's one... or not.
 Jahrome Hughes with a tantalising hung kick from right to left, no one from Australia reads it and Ronaldo Mulitalo charges through. The centre gives New Zealand just a glimmer of hope.
 And the glimmer is dashed, as the video replay shows Mulitalo did not gather it cleanly. It is ruled a knock on.
 Oh well.

 Kalyn Ponga leads a promising New Zealand attack - and has his shorts pulled down as he is tackled!
 New Zealand being pantsed by Australia, figuratively and literally.

 Some may view the World Cup as pointless, but one team does have to set the bar for the rest. It’s up to all other countries the rise to the challenge and be inspired by the dominance of Australia!
 Sam H, Warrington

 Post published at 53 mins 53 mins 
 Australia 28-6 New Zealand 
 More bad news for New Zealand - Casey McLean has failed a head injury assessment following a blow earlier in this half.
 McLean was impressive for New Zealand early doors, but will not return to this match.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Australia 28-6 New Zealand 
 Jack Bostock is so close to claiming a kick over to the left of the goal area, but cannot quite gather it in.
 Relentless from Australia.

 Post published at 51 mins 51 mins 
 Australia 28-6 New Zealand 
 This is as one-sided as any of the blowout group stage matches.
 Australia rip apart the New Zealand defence, before Xavier Willison makes a superb tackle just before the line.
 Willison then drops the ball immediately from the set restart. Schoolboy error.

 I love rugby league, I think it's probably the most exciting, fast and physical sport in the world. However, an international World Cup is pointless. Australia have won all bar two - maybe a Club World Cup would be the way to go in four years time.
 David, Morecambe

 Post published at 47 mins 47 mins 
 Australia 28-6 New Zealand 
 Australia have not lost a men's World Cup match since the 2008 final - 23 tournament matches ago.
 It looks almost certain now that the run will continue.
 Image source, Getty Images

 Post published at 46 mins 46 mins 
 Australia 28-6 New Zealand 
 That was magnificent from Reece Walsh, who has been pretty much perfect all night. The star boy for Australia has risen to the occasion, repaying Kevin Walters' faith in picking him at full back ahead of James Tedesco.
 Walsh may also have been stung at missing out on the Golden Boot for player of the year to Kalyn Ponga.

 Post published at 09:48 GMT 09:48 GMT 
 Australia 28-6 New Zealand 
 Paul Rowley 
Castleford Tigers head coach on BBC Radio 5 Sports Extra 
 I spoke about the sequence of events that leads to Australia's tries. 
 It's too easy. Disappointing for New Zealand. 
 4 3 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 TRY - Australia 28-6 New Zealand published at 09:47 GMT 09:47 GMT 
 Tom Trbojevic (44 mins) 
 That might be game over.
 Reece Walsh shows his immense quality by shrugging off two tackles before laying off under the third, allowing Tom Trbojevic to score.
 Cameron Munster misses from the tee, but Australia have opened a chasm.
 Image source, Getty Images 
 11 10 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 43 mins 43 mins 
 Australia 24-6 New Zealand 
 A bomb from Australia seems certain to lead to a try for Reece Walsh down the left, but Dane Gagai manages to tip it out.
 Australia will come again.
 9 1 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Post published at 09:45 GMT 09:45 GMT 
 Australia 24-6 New Zealand 
 Australia head coach Kevin Walters, speaking on Premier Sports: "It was a very fast start. Both teams are trying to play fast footy, which is great. We've got to make sure we continue with strong defence. The offloads caused havoc - and we want to focus on the last play options, making sure we turn the ball over when we want to turn it over."

 Australia 24-6 New Zealand 
 Erin Clark knocks on during New Zealand's first move of the second half.
 Another false start, another error.
